old: went down some stairs
new: went downward
reason: Source says only 'I walked and, I believe, descended'; 'stairs' is an invented detail the Creature could not know.

old: Darkness troubled me, but then I found that by opening my eyes, light poured in again.
new: Darkness then came over me and troubled me, but I had hardly felt it when the light poured in on me again — because, as I now suppose, I had opened my eyes.
reason: Source hedges 'by opening my eyes, as I now suppose'; the candidate turns a later guess into something he 'found' at the time.

old: It seemed as divine a retreat to me then as the finest palace.
new: To me then it seemed as exquisite and divine a retreat as Pandæmonium, the palace of hell, seemed to the demons after their suffering in the lake of fire.
reason: Source compares the hut to 'Pandæmonium ... to the dæmons of hell after their sufferings in the lake of fire' (a Paradise Lost allusion central to the Creature's later self-image); 'the finest palace' deletes it. [lead: source spelling Pandæmonium kept]

old: from the snow, rain, and cruelty of men.
new: from the snow and rain.
reason: Source 15.9 ends 'from the snow and rain'; 'cruelty of men' is pulled forward from 15.10, which already renders 'the barbarity of man'.

old: It backed up against my hovel. On the exposed sides, a pigsty and a clear pool of water surrounded it.
new: My hovel stood against the back of the cottage, and its exposed sides were bordered by a pigsty and a clear pool of water.
reason: Source: the hovel 'was situated against the back of the cottage and surrounded on the sides which were exposed by a pig sty and a clear pool'; candidate makes the cottage the subject surrounded by the sty and pool.

old: I crept from my hiding place
new: I crept from my kennel
reason: Source's self-deprecating image 'crept from my kennel' is flattened to 'hiding place'.

old: obviously struggling with the weight
new: seemingly burdened by the weight
reason: Source hedges 'seemingly incommoded by the burden'; 'obviously' raises certainty.

old: sweeter than any birdsong I'd heard
new: sweeter than the song of the thrush or the nightingale
reason: Source names 'the voice of the thrush or the nightingale'; the named birds are dropped.

old: The two younger ones often went hungry.
new: The two younger ones, I believe, often went painfully hungry.
reason: Source hedges 'They often, I believe, suffered the pangs of hunger very poignantly'; hedge dropped.

old: after spending many months in my hovel
new: after spending several months in my hovel
reason: Source 'several revolutions of the moon'; 'many' overstates.

old: During the day he sometimes worked for a neighboring farmer, since he often left and came back without firewood.
new: During the day, I believe, he sometimes worked for a neighboring farmer, since he often went out and didn't return until dinner, yet brought no wood with him.
reason: Source 'In the day, I believe, he worked sometimes ... because he often went forth and did not return until dinner, yet brought no wood'; hedge and 'not until dinner' evidence dropped.

old: her path to the cowshed
new: her path to the dairy
reason: Source 'milk-house' is a dairy (where milk is kept), not a cowshed.

old: when it wasn't raining — which happened frequently.
new: when it wasn't raining — that, I found, was what they called it when water poured from the sky. This happened frequently.
reason: Source 'when it did not rain, as I found it was called when the heavens poured forth its waters' records the Creature learning the word; dropped.

old: I thought — foolishly — that
new: I thought — foolish wretch! — that
reason: Source '(foolish wretch!)' is the Creature's own epithet for himself; 'foolishly' removes it.

old: the most important part of my story
new: the more moving part of my story
reason: Source 'the more moving part of my story'; 'most important' changes the claim.

old: Being base and vicious seemed
new: Being base and vicious, as many people in history have been, seemed
reason: Source 'to be base and vicious, as many on record have been'; clause dropped.

old: I was also cursed with a hideously deformed body.
new: I was also cursed with a hideously deformed and loathsome body.
reason: Source 'a figure hideously deformed and loathsome'; 'loathsome' dropped.

old: I was faster and could survive
new: I was more agile than they were and could survive
reason: Source 'more agile'; agility is not speed.

old: It was a story that couldn't fail to make a deep impression on someone as utterly inexperienced as I was.
new: It was a story that couldn't fail to make a deep impression on me, since it revealed a number of circumstances, each one interesting and wonderful to someone as utterly inexperienced as I was.
reason: Source 'unfolding as it did a number of circumstances, each interesting and wonderful to one so utterly inexperienced'; the reason is dropped.

old: that virtue, intelligence, and a moderate fortune could provide
new: that virtue, a refined intellect, or taste, together with a moderate fortune, could provide
reason: Source 'virtue, refinement of intellect, or taste, accompanied by a moderate fortune'; 'taste' dropped.

old: The day set for the Turk's execution arrived, but the night before, he escaped from prison.
new: The day of the Turk's execution was set, but on the night before it he escaped from prison.
reason: Source 'The day for the execution ... was fixed'; 'arrived' misstates the sequence (he escaped before the day came).

old: over the Alps to Leghorn
new: across Mont Cenis, a pass over the Alps, to Leghorn
reason: Source names 'across Mont Cenis'; proper place name dropped (brief gloss keeps it clear aloud).

old: to help with some future plan.
new: to help him, as the Turk put it, with some plan for supporting himself in the future.
reason: Source 'to aid him, as he said, in some plan of future maintenance'; the ironic 'as he said' is lost.

old: told her urgently that his hiding place in Leghorn had been discovered
new: told her urgently that he had reason to believe his hiding place in Leghorn had been revealed
reason: Source 'he had reason to believe that his residence at Leghorn had been divulged'; certainty raised.

old: He planned to leave his daughter with a trusted servant, who would follow later with most of his property
new: He planned to leave his daughter in the care of a trusted servant; she would follow at her leisure with most of his property
reason: Source: the daughter was 'to follow at her leisure with the greater part of his property'; candidate makes the servant follow — actor change.

old: about sixty miles from
new: about twenty leagues from
reason: Source 'twenty leagues'; candidate keeps 'leagues' elsewhere (18.8), so the silent unit conversion is inconsistent.

old: happened in early August.
new: happened in early August of that same year.
reason: Source 'the beginning of the month of August of the same year'; time anchor dropped.

old: _The Sorrows of Young Werther_
new: _The Sorrows of Werter_
reason: Source prints '_Sorrows of Werter_'; RULES forbid correcting source names to standard forms (and 'Young' is added).

old: _The Sorrows of Werther_
new: _The Sorrows of Werter_
reason: Source spells 'Werter'; do not normalize.

old: But I thought Werther himself a more magnificent being
new: But I thought Werter himself a more godlike being
reason: Source 'Werter himself a more divine being'; spelling normalized and 'divine' weakened to 'magnificent'.

old: Its descriptions of gentle domestic life and lofty feeling matched
new: Its descriptions of gentle domestic life, together with lofty feelings directed at something beyond the self, matched
reason: Source 'lofty sentiments and feelings, which had for their object something out of self'; the key qualifier is dropped.

old: from the people I read about.
new: from the people I read about and the people whose conversation I listened to.
reason: Source 'the beings concerning whom I read and to whose conversation I was a listener'; second half dropped.

old: These questions kept returning, answered only by groans.
new: These questions kept returning, but I couldn't answer them.
reason: Source 'These questions continually recurred, but I was unable to solve them'; 'answered only by groans' is imported from 17.20.

old: _Plutarch's Lives_ had a very different effect. From Werther
new: The volume of _Plutarch's Lives_ that I had contained the histories of the first founders of the ancient republics. This book had a very different effect on me from _The Sorrows of Werter_. From Werter
reason: Source opening sentence 'contained the histories of the first founders of the ancient republics' is missing, and 'Werter' is normalized.

old: I kept postponing it — the stakes
new: I postponed it for some months longer — the stakes
reason: Source 'I postponed this attempt for some months longer'; duration dropped.

old: Safie's presence had spread happiness.
new: Safie's presence had spread happiness, and I also found that the household now had more plenty than before.
reason: Source 'I also found that a greater degree of plenty reigned there' is omitted.

old: the trial I'd resolved to face.
new: the trial I'd resolved to face in a few months.
reason: Source 'the trial which in a few months I resolved to undergo'; timing dropped.

old: when I first saw the woods.
new: when I first saw the woods and the lovely moon.
reason: Source 'when I first beheld the woods and the lovely moon' (callback to 15.2); moon dropped.

old: the more I longed for their acceptance and love.
new: the more I longed to claim their protection and kindness. My heart yearned to be known and loved by these kind people.
reason: Source has two clauses: 'desire to claim their protection and kindness; my heart yearned to be known and loved'; candidate collapses them.

old: So I reasoned that if I could win the old man's goodwill in his children's absence, he might mediate on my behalf with the younger members of the family and prepare them for my appearance.
new: So I reasoned that if, in his children's absence, I could win the goodwill and help of old De Lacey, through him I might be tolerated by my younger protectors.
reason: Source 'I might by his means be tolerated by my younger protectors'; 'prepare them for my appearance' is added and 'tolerated' (a modest hope) is lost.

old: something in your voice
new: something in your words
reason: Source 'something in your words which persuades me'.

old: My family has been condemned
new: My family and I have been condemned
reason: Source 'I and my family have been condemned'.

old: as a lion tears its prey
new: as the lion tears apart the antelope
reason: Source 'as the lion rends the antelope'; image generalized.

old: wouldn't let me rest peacefully
new: wouldn't let me have peaceful dreams
reason: Source 'did not allow me to be visited by peaceful dreams'; the next sentence is the dream, so 'rest' loses the link when heard.

old: That hour came.
new: That hour passed.
reason: Source 'That hour passed'; 'came' reads as if the family then appeared.

old: using animated gestures
new: gesturing violently
reason: Source 'violent gesticulations'; softened.

old: those thoughts vanished into tears that briefly soothed me
new: my thoughts of revenge vanished, and a flood of tears soothed me a little
reason: Source 'these thoughts vanished' refers to the revenge thoughts; candidate reads as if the thoughts of his friends vanished.

old: danced with fury around the cottage
new: danced with fury around the doomed cottage
reason: Source 'the devoted cottage' (i.e., doomed); qualifier dropped.

old: Heartless creator!
new: Unfeeling, heartless creator!
reason: Source 'Unfeeling, heartless creator!'.

old: and from you I was determined to get it.
new: and from you I was determined to get the justice I had tried in vain to gain from every other being in human form.
reason: Source 'that justice which I vainly attempted to gain from any other being that wore the human form'; dropped.

old: toward the blessed sun.
new: toward the blessed sun that gave me such joy.
reason: Source 'the blessed sun, which bestowed such joy upon me'.

old: worsened by the unbearable sense of injustice.
new: worsened by the crushing sense of the injustice and ingratitude behind that wound.
reason: Source 'the oppressive sense of the injustice and ingratitude of their infliction'; 'ingratitude' dropped.

old: It stirred the devil within me.
new: It stirred the fiend within me.
reason: Source 'it stirred the fiend within me'; the Creature's own term.

old: But a creature as deformed and horrible as myself wouldn't refuse me. You must create my companion.
new: But a creature as deformed and horrible as myself wouldn't refuse me. My companion must be of the same species and have the same defects. You must create this being.
reason: Source 'My companion must be of the same species and have the same defects. This being you must create.'; the demand's terms are dropped.

old: The creature finished speaking
new: The being finished speaking
reason: Source 'The being finished speaking'; narrator's term swapped.

old: the creature replied
new: the fiend replied
reason: Source 'replied the fiend'; RULES: neutralizing 'fiend' to 'creature' is a meaning change.

old: and especially toward you, my creator and greatest enemy, I swear undying hatred.
new: and above all toward you, my greatest enemy because you are my creator, I swear undying hatred.
reason: Source 'towards you my arch-enemy, because my creator'; causal link lost.

old: I would return it a hundredfold.
new: I would return it a hundred and a hundredfold.
reason: Source's rhetorical doubling 'a hundred and a hundredfold' is flattened. [lead: closer to source wording]

old: Let me know that I matter to some living being.
new: Let me see that I can awaken sympathy in some living thing.
reason: Source 'Let me see that I excite the sympathy of some existing thing'; 'matter to' changes the plea.

old: He saw my hesitation
new: He saw my change of feeling
reason: Source 'He saw my change of feeling'; 'hesitation' misstates Victor's shift toward sympathy.

old: peaceful and humane. You can only deny it out of cruelty and abuse of power.
new: peaceful and human, and you must feel that you could deny it only out of a wanton abuse of power and cruelty.
reason: Source 'peaceful and human, and you must feel that you could deny it only in the wantonness of power and cruelty'; 'humane' alters 'human' and the appeal to Victor's feeling is dropped.

old: the grotesque mass
new: the filthy mass
reason: Source 'the filthy mass that moved and talked'; Victor's term softened.

old: With that, he suddenly left me.
new: With that, he suddenly left me, afraid, perhaps, that I might change my mind.
reason: Source 'fearful, perhaps, of any change in my sentiments' omitted.

old: among the ridges of the glacier
new: among the waves of the sea of ice
reason: Source 'undulations of the sea of ice'; candidate uses 'sea of ice' elsewhere (14.4, 26.7) for this recurring place.

old: as if it were a deadly storm coming to consume me
new: as if it were a dull, ugly sirocco — the hot desert wind — on its way to consume me
reason: Source 'a dull ugly siroc on its way to consume me'; the specific image is replaced; brief gloss keeps it clear aloud.
